writeup: TIC 441012538 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 4.84 days, detected in TESS photometry with a signal-to-noise ratio of 151. The primary eclipse produces a 4.26 percent dimming, while no secondary eclipse was detected. Pixel-level analysis confirms the signal at the target location with a peak signal-to-noise of 39.4, though the centroid offset of 5.5 arcseconds warrants attention. The system does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs. However, analysis reveals that successive eclipses differ significantly in depth, suggesting the initial analysis underestimated the true orbital period by a factor of two. This data quality flag indicates an underlying periodicity of 4.84 days rather than the initially measured value, a correction supported by the pixel-level confirmation and eclipse timing measurements.
